 The Los Angeles Lakers come into their game against the Utah Jazz on Wednesday evening looking to extend the league's current active win streak of nine games, and they'll have a near perfect slate of health. Austin Reaves remained out on the Lakers' injury report Wednesday afternoon, but there were no other names listed. That means Walker Kessler was cleared to make his return to the Lakers' lineup after missing the comeback win against the Charlotte Hornets , his first missed game of the season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That also meant that Luka Doncic would be available for the Lakers on the second night of a back-to-back. Doncic has missed two games this season, both during a set of back-to-back games, as the Lakers continue to manage his back issues. But with the team holding the best record in the NBA at 13-2, they will have their MVP candidate available.
 Doncic is leading the league in scoring at 38.8 points to go along with 7.2 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.8 steals. He's shooting 47.6 percent from the field, 39.8 percent from the 3-point line and 85.7 percent from the free-throw line.

 In Reaves' case, Lakers head coach JJ Redick mentioned prior to the Hornets game that the plan was to see how Reaves felt in the morning ahead of the Jazz game, and to try and get him some on-court work if possible. Redick has also made it clear that Reaves has not suffered any structural damage, that it's a bruise that is more about pain tolerance.
 Click Here to Subscribe Fresh off a new four-year $180 million contract extension, Reaves had only missed one game this year prior to the injury, due to illness, and he had been playing at an All-Star level. The 28-year-old guard had been averaging a career best 24.7 points. 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals with splits of 51.3 percent shooting from the field, 40.9 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 91.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line.
